facts.text: This opening newscast was originally going to be on-screen text only. Writer-director Jay Lee's fake news about a fourth George W. Bush term sets up the film's political satire.
Zombie Strippers began as a joke. Director Jay Lee, making a horror film called The Slaughter, quipped about making 'Zombie Strippers' instead, then found nobody had used the title.
Jay Lee wrote, directed AND shot this movie as his own cinematographer, partly to save money. His sister Angela Lee produced it.
The whole film cost about one million dollars and was shot in just eighteen days. Jay Lee aimed for roughly 70 camera setups a day.
Jay Lee says he never wrote a synopsis for the film and suspects some of the backers approved it without even reading the script.
Robert Englund (Freddy Krueger) dyed his hair white so he wouldn't look too much like himself. He told Classic-Horror: "There's a wink there. You know it's me."
Robert Englund's strip club owner is named Ian Essko, a pun on absurdist playwright Eugène Ionesco, whose play Rhinoceros inspired the film. The club is called Rhino's.
Robert Englund told Classic-Horror he played Ian Essko as a sleazy buffoon who "doesn't like women" and sees his strippers as scum, even while running a strip club.
Jenna Jameson was the first person the filmmakers approached. Jay Lee's sister, producer Angela Lee, got her the script; Jameson liked its mix of horror, comedy and political statement.
The club bouncer is MMA fighter Tito Ortiz, then Jenna Jameson's boyfriend. They later had twin sons, born in March 2009.
The actresses choreographed their own striptease routines, and crew members doubled as extras in the club crowd.
Joanna Pacula was originally cast as Madame Blavatski but left over a schedule conflict, and later regretted it. The role was specifically written for Carmit Levité.
Roxy Saint, who plays goth stripper Lillith, also performed several songs on the soundtrack, including "Smother You," heard again over the end credits.
Jay Lee on nudity in horror: "I actually don't think it's that essential," though he admits that given two DVDs, he'd probably rent the one with nudity.
Zombie Strippers was a spoof of The Warriors (1979): a zombie taunts "Warriors, come out to play," the line made famous by David Patrick Kelly as Luther.
The first infected Marine is named Byrdflough, a pun on bird flu.
Actress Shamron Moore told Boomtron the cast hadn't read Rhinoceros, so director Jay Lee sometimes had to explain the Ionesco references. She had originally read for the role of Kat.
Shamron Moore told Boomtron the Jeannie-vs-Kat fight was hard to film: she struggled to keep a straight face while Jenna Jameson hurled objects at her head.
Robert Englund told Classic-Horror the movie was a "punk-rock reaction" to bloated, over-produced films, a nod to 70s and 80s exploitation and early Sam Raimi.
Penny Drake (Penny Vital), who plays stripper Sox, later appeared at E3 in 2009 as video game heroine Bayonetta, and was in Sin City and The 40 Year Old Virgin.
Robert Englund reportedly cut his hand during filming. Director Jay Lee praised his professionalism: he covered the injury with makeup and kept working.
Roxy Saint's pierced nipples in the film were done with prosthetic make-up.
Richard Scheib of Moria called Robert Englund's performance "perpetually awful" but said it suits the film's tone. He gave the movie three stars.
Richard Scheib of Moria praised Jay Lee's "appealing sarcasm," comparing the opening Marine sequence to Aliens (1986), but played for absurd laughs.
Rotten Tomatoes gives Zombie Strippers 38%, with the consensus: "never rises above its silly premise." Richard Roeper said it "doesn't work as camp." Variety called it a "one-joke pic."
The Hollywood Reporter's Michael Rechtshaffen found something "perversely affecting" in the film, despite its "lame political satire."
The Stranger compared the film to the "blood, beasts, and breasts" gospel of drive-in critic Joe Bob Briggs, and found it just wasn't any fun.
Sony gave the film a limited theatrical release on April 18, 2008. The Numbers lists its worldwide take at only $8,259; Box Office Mojo lists about $82,000.
The film's theatrical release pushed the DVD from spring to October 2008. Sony let Jay Lee add many deleted scenes back in, giving several characters more resolution.
The R-rated theatrical cut was trimmed of nudity and gore to avoid an NC-17; the unrated version restores it. Germany's "not under 18" cut removes much of the violence.
Jay Lee said he'd love to direct Jessica Alba or Jessica Biel as zombie strippers.
Jenna Jameson announced her retirement from porn at the 2008 AVN Awards, the year this film came out. She'd won over 35 adult-video awards and crossed over with Howard Stern's Private Parts (1997).
Robert Englund's other directing credits include 976-EVIL (1988) and Killer Pad (2008). He is best known as Freddy Krueger in eight Elm Street films.
Scream 4 (2011) and the found-footage horror film The Houses October Built (2014) both reference Zombie Strippers.
The film nods to Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan, The Boondock Saints and The Treasure of the Sierra Madre ("We don't need no stinking badgers!"), and spoofs UHF.
Jenna Jameson's first striptease in the film was shot with two cameras. Zombie Strippers was also the screen debut of actress Kateland Carr.
Richard Scheib of Moria places the film in the wave of comic zombie movies after Shaun of the Dead (2004), noting a near-twin rival, Zombies! Zombies! Zombies! (2008).
Production company Stage 6 Films, formed in 2007, is a Sony Pictures label named after the Culver City soundstage where The Wizard of Oz was shot.
The film's tagline was "Live Dead Nudes."
